topic: measles outbreak as immunisation wake-up call
headline_marked: Nearly 900 suspected dead in [[Bangladesh measles outbreak]]
headline: Nearly 900 suspected dead in Bangladesh measles outbreak
summary: A severe outbreak primarily affecting children has sparked a nationwide emergency vaccination campaign to prevent further deaths.
details: Almost 900 people, mostly children, are suspected to have died in a measles outbreak in Bangladesh that began in March 2026. The disease spread rapidly due to falling vaccination rates and gaps in protection.
Between March 15 and September 6, 2026, the country reported 92 suspected measles cases per 100,000 people and 11 confirmed cases per 100,000, based on a population of 178 million.

The crisis is attributed to disrupted routine childhood vaccinations during the COVID-19 pandemic and political instability, with overall coverage sliding to 87%. Vaccine hesitancy among parents also played a role.

In response, the government launched an emergency vaccination campaign in April for children aged six months to five years. Following WHO advice, an additional dose was given to all children in this group regardless of prior vaccination.

The Directorate General of Health Services activated rapid response teams and increased isolation beds in hospitals, where pediatric wards filled with children suffering from high fever, rash, and breathing difficulties.

Every child with suspected or confirmed measles received vitamin A to lower the risk of severe illness. UNICEF, WHO, and Gavi supported the government, while Save the Children conducted community awareness drives.

Health experts warn that risks remain if routine booster shots are missed or if rumors continue to discourage vaccination. Because measles is highly contagious, widespread immunity is essential to break the chain of infection.

topic: PM addresses UNGA on climate change
headline_marked: PM takes [[climate fight to UN]], UNGA debut in focus
headline: PM takes climate fight to UN, UNGA debut in focus
summary: The Prime Minister's first address to the United Nations General Assembly will prioritize climate action and global cooperation.
details: The Prime Minister is set to make his debut appearance at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), focusing heavily on the global climate crisis.
A key priority for the visit is to advocate for stronger climate action and more effective support for vulnerable nations facing environmental threats.
The address is expected to highlight Bangladesh's role as a climate-vulnerable country and the push for global accountability in climate financing.
The Prime Minister's debut at the UNGA will also serve as a platform to engage with world leaders to discuss bilateral relations and international cooperation.
caption:
Bangladesh's Prime Minister is heading to the UN to lead the charge on climate action.

The Prime Minister is set to make his debut appearance at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), focusing heavily on the global climate crisis.

A key priority for the visit is to advocate for stronger climate action and more effective support for vulnerable nations facing environmental threats.

The address is expected to highlight Bangladesh's role as a climate-vulnerable country and the push for global accountability in climate financing.

The Prime Minister's debut at the UNGA will also serve as a platform to engage with world leaders to discuss bilateral relations and international cooperation.
